## Aim

To test the manufacturer's claim that the median breaking strength of the rods is 30 pounds using the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test at the 1% level of significance.

## Practical

The breaking strength (in pounds) of a random sample of 29 rods made by a manufacturer is given as follows:

$$
19,30,28,35,23,37,36,32,40,24,
$$

$$
31,33,21,36,30,32,26,40,38,28,
$$

$$
30,41,22,43,25,28,24,37,17.
$$

On the basis of this sample, test the manufacturer's claim that the median breaking strength of the rods is 30 pounds using the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test at the 1% level of significance. Assume that the distribution of the breaking strengths is symmetric about its median.

## Theory

The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test is a non-parametric test used to test a population median.

Let \(M\) denote the population median breaking strength.

The hypotheses are:

$$
H_0: M = 30
$$

against

$$
H_1: M \neq 30
$$

For each observation \(X_i\), calculate the difference

$$
d_i = X_i - 30.
$$

The observations for which \(d_i=0\) are omitted. The absolute differences

$$
|d_i|
$$

are ranked from smallest to largest, with average ranks assigned to tied values. The signs of the original differences are then attached to the corresponding ranks.

The Wilcoxon signed-rank statistic is based on the sum of the positive and negative ranks.

The level of significance is

$$
\alpha = 0.01.
$$

Decision rule:

- If \(p\text{-value} < 0.01\), we may reject \(H_0\).
- If \(p\text{-value} \geq 0.01\), we may not reject \(H_0\).

## Code

```{r}
# Data
breaking_strength <- c(
  19, 30, 28, 35, 23, 37, 36, 32, 40, 24,
  31, 33, 21, 36, 30, 32, 26, 40, 38, 28,
  30, 41, 22, 43, 25, 28, 24, 37, 17
)

# Hypothesized median
mu0 <- 30

# Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test
result <- wilcox.test(
  breaking_strength,
  mu = mu0,
  alternative = "two.sided",
  exact = FALSE
)

result

```

## Results

The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test was performed to test the hypothesis

$$
H_0: M = 30
$$

against

$$
H_1: M \neq 30
$$

The test statistic obtained is $V = 193$ and the corresponding p-value is $p\text{-value} = 0.6654$

Since $p\text{-value} > \alpha = 0.01,$ we may not reject the null hypothesis.

## Conclusion

At the $1\%$ level of significance, there is not sufficient evidence to conclude that the population median breaking strength of the rods differs from $30$ pounds.

Hence, we conclude that the median breaking strength of the rods can be regarded as $30$ pounds.
